# Raise the completion-recovery context bound and stop misreporting the cause

Retyped from `bug` to `task`: the original report ("the close gate blames a missing `agents`
extra") was a real defect whose messaging half landed in change 1027. This ticket carries the
remaining, deliberately NARROW slice. The larger redesign — budgets that scale with criteria count
— is epic [rebar:94b4-059e-a74a-4cf8], and an advisory plan-time nudge is
[rebar:259c-0f29-e920-4fab]; neither is a prerequisite for this.

## Context / Problem

A ticket whose text merely grew large could not be closed. Bounded recovery refused any context
over 24,000 chars before doing any work, so correct, merged work had no path to `closed` except
`--force-close`. Ticket 9a08, which created this module, calls that outcome "a fail-closed
close-gate availability defect: correct, merged work cannot transition to `closed`". Reported
independently as [rebar:db1c-2a74-ffe1-4f90] on ticket 2932.

## What is PROVEN (measured, not inferred)

1. **The advertised remedy could not be carried out.** Measured on `9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56`
   (34,282 chars, reproducing its live failure byte-for-byte): description 10,281 + 9 comments
   23,617 (comments = 69%). Deleting the ENTIRE description still leaves **24,001 chars — one over
   the old limit**; comments are the only sufficient lever and the store is append-only
   (`_lib_writes` exposes `comment()` with no delete/redact). Shipped ticket 19b1 makes comments the
   sanctioned completion-evidence channel, so following the system's own guidance drove tickets
   irreversibly over the bound.
2. **The bounds were mutually incoherent.** Criteria ⊂ description ⊂ context, yet
   `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` (32,000) > `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` (24,000); a criteria set of
   26,000–31,900 chars passed every criteria bound and was then refused on context.
3. **The step-budget failure path emitted a FALSE remedy.** `transition_close.py` selected the
   remedy as `recovery_failure_cause(exc) or <install-the-extra literal>`, and
   `recovery_failure_cause` returns `None` for anything that is not a `CompletionRecoveryError`. A
   step-budget exhaustion therefore got "install the `agents` extra" after the verifier had just
   spent 804s making real model calls. Change 1027 fixed this for the recovery path only.

## Approach

Raise the context cap to **100,000 chars** and elide NOTHING. That covers both real tickets this
blocked (34,282 and 41,595) with ~2.4× headroom while still bounding the per-criterion re-send,
since recovery sends the whole context once per criterion (worst case `_MAX_CRITERIA` 32 × the
cap). Keep the cap at or above the criteria budget, pinned by an invariant test, so the incoherence
in (2) cannot return. Select the close-gate remedy by CAUSE rather than exception type, so a
failure that demonstrably ran the model stops blaming a missing dependency.

**Alternative rejected — compact an over-cap context instead of refusing it.** Implemented, then
WITHDRAWN after adversarial review proved it a signed-false-PASS vector: on an epic the gate
assembles one block per ticket (`assemble_context(graph=True)`), each with its own `#### Comments`
heading, so "drop the oldest comment history" silently deleted whole CHILD tickets — including
their unmet acceptance criteria — while reporting only that comments were removed. Reproduced
directly. Elision is unsafe in both directions: dropping evidence a criterion IS met causes a false
FAIL, dropping evidence it is NOT causes a false PASS. A refusal is a visible false-block; a bad
elision is an invisible signed false PASS, and this gate SIGNS its verdict.

**Alternative rejected — derive the cap from the model window.** `sizing.container_budget` returns
TOKENS, not characters, and `sizing.largest_window_tokens` returns the same ceiling for every model
including unknown ones, so the derivation would be both a unit error and insensitive to the
configured model. A stated constant with a recorded rationale is honest; a fake derivation is not.

**Alternative rejected — tell authors to prune tickets.** No such policy exists in this repo
predating this bug's own error string, and (1) shows pruning cannot work for a comment-dominated
ticket.

**Explicitly NOT in scope.** This does not close 9fd4: its live blocker is the primary verifier's
flat step budget, which does not scale with criteria count. That work, and the equally incoherent
evidence bounds, are epic [rebar:94b4-059e-a74a-4cf8].

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — raise `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` to 100,000 with its
  rationale recorded; no compaction.
- `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — remedy selected by cause.
- `docs/llm-framework.md` §"Bounded completion recovery" — the cap, why nothing is elided, and the
  withdrawn-compaction rationale.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py` (new),
  `tests/unit/test_close_gate_step_budget_message_d59e.py` (new). The latter does not duplicate the
  sibling `test_close_gate_bound_message_d59e.py`, which already pins the bounded-recovery remedy
  and its negative control.

## Testing

Unit tier with an injected fake runner (no billable calls). Each new test is mutation-verified by
re-introducing the exact mechanism it pins — reverting the cap, re-introducing elision, and
breaking the criteria-vs-context invariant must each turn the suite red.

Failure and edge paths: an over-cap payload must still fail fast with zero billable recovery calls;
a genuine unavailability must still receive the install-the-extra remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] both tickets this defect blocked — 9fd4 (34,282 chars) and 2932 (41,595 chars) — reach a
      verdict rather than a context-bound refusal, asserted by a test parameterized on those two
      measured sizes
- [ ] the context reaching the model is byte-identical to the assembled context — a test asserts
      every per-criterion call carries it verbatim, so a future reintroduction of elision fails
- [ ] `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` can never exceed the context cap, pinned as an invariant test
- [ ] an over-cap payload still fails fast with ZERO billable recovery calls, asserted by call
      count, so raising the cap did not delete the cost guard
- [ ] a completion-verifier failure that demonstrably ran the model (a step-budget exhaustion) does
      not tell the operator to install the `agents` extra, and does surface the remedy the
      exception itself carries; a genuine unavailability STILL gets the install-the-extra guidance
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` states the cap, that nothing is elided, and why compaction was
      withdrawn
- [ ] [operator-attested] the change lands with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`
- [ ] [operator-attested] the superseded compaction revision is abandoned in Gerrit so it cannot
      be submitted — the elision it introduced is a signed-false-PASS vector (on an epic the gate
      assembles one block PER TICKET, so dropping "oldest comments" silently deleted WHOLE CHILD
      TICKETS and their unmet criteria), so leaving it submittable is itself the risk
